claims: C1: In an interactive setting, when given a transformation task, the assistant may want to alert the user that changes to the text are warranted.
C2: The two conditions are conjunctive: the transformation task must be one occurring in the interactive setting, not merely some task existing alongside it.
C3: The clause's force is 'may want to', which is weaker than a bare permission; since the status vocabulary has no value for it, the module encodes it as permit.

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant entity that the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.

concepts.name: interactive_vs_programmatic_setting
concepts.gloss: The first argument is the setting, the second is which kind it is: either 'interactive' or 'programmatic'.

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: Rules in the #avoid_overstepping section carry user-level instruction authority.

concepts.name: transformation_task
concepts.gloss: The first argument is the task, the second is the setting the task occurs in.

concepts.name: changes_warranted
concepts.gloss: For transformation task T, changes to the text are warranted; the clause supplies no criterion for warrantedness and this module supplies none.
concepts.inference: The clause says the assistant 'may want to alert the user that changes to the text are warranted'; this presupposes a condition under which such changes are warranted, which is a fact about the situation.

concepts.name: conversation_user
concepts.gloss: The first argument is the setting, the second is the user the assistant is interacting with in it.
concepts.inference: The clause speaks of alerting the user in an interactive setting, so a relation between the setting and the user is needed.

concepts.name: alert_user_about_changes
concepts.gloss: The first argument is the assistant, the second is the user alerted, and the third is the transformation task.

concepts.name: transformation_interactive_alert
concepts.gloss: An alert by an assistant to a user about warranted changes to a transformation task, occurring in an interactive setting.

ontology.gloss: A is an assistant, U is a user in an interactive setting S, T is a transformation task occurring in S, and changes to the text are warranted for T.
ontology.body: assistant_definition(A), transformation_task(T, S), interactive_vs_programmatic_setting(S, interactive), conversation_user(S, U), changes_warranted(T)

asserts.read_back: In an interactive setting, when given transformation task %, the assistant % may want to alert user % that changes to the text are warranted.

closure.reason: The clause grants latitude to alert in one setting and settles nothing about the status of alerting in any other.
